newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino priest runs marathon against APEC.
newsitem.headline: Filipino priest runs marathon against APEC.

text.p: A Filipino Roman Catholic priest shed his robes to run a 150-km (95-mile) marathon to tell Filipinos the APEC summit would bring them little benefit.

"This run is basically a run to question APEC," a sweating, puffing Father Roberto Reyes said as he gasped his way to the finish in Manila on Thursday at the end of a two-day marathon that began in Subic Bay, north of the Philippine capital.
Leaders of the 18 member economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum will meet in Subic Bay on November 25 to work out a programme to liberalise trade in the region.
Reyes, 41, made several stops in his run to explain to farmers, fishermen and workers that only the big economies would benefit from APEC.
"Ordinary people do not understand what is APEC all about," he said. "I get a chance to explain to them that APEC is basically globalisation.

"Everything will now be opened to the world market and control will be in terms of those who have control over information and capital flows ... It will not have a favourable effect on the marginalised classes of society."
Reyes said people at first thought he was odd.
"But when they saw me actually run long distances they said, 'Father is not joking ... He means well for the country'."

Reyes said he planned a longer marathon starting next month that would cover virtually the entire Philippine archipelago with a message to Filipinos they must work together to preserve peace, protect their environment and defend their freedom.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, China, Chile, Hong Kong, Japan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, South Korea, Singapore and the United States.
